learningObjective: Diagnose why an autotuner-chosen tile size regressed on a new shape and identify the trade-off that triggered it.
profileData:
Original tuned config: block=128×128, warp=64×64. Peak on M=N=K=4096: 82% TC utilization.
Same config on M=N=K=1024 shape: 34% TC utilization, only 8 blocks in grid, ~ 24 SMs idle on A100 (108 SMs).
Test of block=64×64 config on M=N=K=1024: 71% TC utilization, 256 blocks, all SMs busy.
stem: An autotuned GEMM tile of block=128×128 is optimal at M=N=K=4096 but regresses to 34% TC utilization at M=N=K=1024. Retuning with block=64×64 recovers to 71%. Which trade-off is the primary cause?

options.text: At the smaller shape, the 128×128 tile produces too few grid blocks to fill all 108 SMs on A100; parallelism, not per-tile arithmetic intensity, becomes the bottleneck.
The 128×128 tile causes register spills at smaller shapes; smaller tiles avoid the spill and recover throughput.
A100 Tensor Cores require tile sizes that are exact multiples of 128 in each dimension; 1024 is not a valid choice for 128 tiles.
The autotuner overfit to M=4096 hardware calibration; the same 128×128 tile is still optimal at 1024 but Nsight Compute misreports utilization on small grids.

explanation: For a 1024×1024 GEMM with 128×128 tiles, the grid is (1024/128)² = 64 blocks in the M-N plane before splitK; assuming no split-K, only 64 blocks are launched. A100 has 108 SMs; without persistent-kernel or split-K strategies, roughly 44 SMs are idle. Halving the tile to 64×64 yields 256 blocks — 2.4× the SM count — which restores full SM occupancy and lifts effective throughput. This is the canonical 'tile-too-big for small shapes' regression. Register spills or Tensor-Core divisibility (1024 IS a multiple of 128) are not the issue; the autotuner did not misreport utilization, it simply chose parameters for a different workload.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: too-few grid blocks under-utilize SMs at the smaller shape.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no spill evidence is given; the profile shows idle SMs, not spill.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: 1024 IS a multiple of 128; TC does not require this level of divisibility.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: 34% TC utilization on an under-populated grid is a real signal, not a mis-report.

assumptions: No split-K is enabled in the original config.
Tensor Core M×N×K = 16×16×16 (or larger) is compatible with both 64×64 and 128×128 blocks.
nonImplications: Does not imply the fix must be 64×64; alternatives include enabling split-K, persistent kernels, or shape-specialized tuning.
Does not imply block=128×128 is always suboptimal — at M=N=K=4096 it was the winner.

distractorRationales.B: Invents a spill without profile support.
distractorRationales.D: Blames the profiler for a real workload mismatch.

sourceRefs.locator: Section on shape-specialized tuning and tile-size search

performanceClaim.scope: Tile-size / grid-count trade-off on A100 GEMM at small shape
